concept: The model is stateless; the harness re-sends the whole conversation on every request.
source_note: The Module 1 investigate scenario, replayed by the course's mini-harness. Sizes use the course's estimate of about 4 characters per token.

item.label: You: Why is the login test failing?

session.explain: You ask a question. The harness builds request 1 from its system prompt, its tool definitions, and your message. The conversation is just a list the harness owns.
The harness sends request 1. The model replies with a request for a tool, never a result: it asks to read the failing test. Its reply joins the conversation.
The harness, not the model, reads the file. Every action happens in harness code, as your user. That is where controls belong.
The whole test file comes back as a tool result, which is ordinary text in the conversation. It will be re-sent on every request from here on.
Request 2 jumps in size, because the test file is now in the history. The model kept nothing from request 1; it reads everything again. Now it asks to run the tests.
Before running a command, this harness asks you: allow `python3 run_tests.py -q`? A denial would not be an error. The model would receive "Permission denied by user." and reason about it.
The test output comes back. One test fails.
Request 3 carries both tool results. The model asks to search for the function under test, but this harness only has read_file and run_command.
The harness has no search tool. It still has to answer with something.
The answer is the text "Unknown tool: search", and that answer becomes context too. Models can ask for tools that do not exist.
Request 4. The model adapts and asks to read the source file directly.
The source file is appended. The conversation is now close to eight times the size of request 1.

item.label: Model: Found it. auth.py returns True for an empty hash. I haven't changed anything.

session.explain: Request 5 is sent. This time the reply has no tool requests, which is the loop's only exit. The model reports the bug and stops.

steps.text: You ask why the login test is failing. The harness builds request 1: its system prompt, its tool definitions, and your message. That is everything the model will see.
The harness sends request 1. The model cannot open files. It replies with a request: read the failing test.
The harness runs the tool. The whole test file comes back and is appended to the conversation.
Request 2 carries everything again: system prompt, tools, your question, the model's tool call, and the test file. The model kept nothing from request 1.
The model asked for a search tool this harness does not have. The harness answers anyway, and "Unknown tool: search" becomes part of the conversation.
By the time the model reports the bug, five requests have been sent. Each one carried everything before it.

predict.question: Request 1 was {first_request} tokens. This session sends five requests. How big is request 5?
predict.reveal: Request 5 is {last_request} tokens, about {growth} times request 1, because it carries everything from requests 1 to 4. Across all five requests the harness sent {total_input} tokens of input. The token growth section looks at that total.
